stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image support.

stories.title: The End of Consensus Research?
stories.author: Martijn de Vos
bullet_points: The paper addresses the long-standing, fundamental problem of consensus in distributed computing and State Machine Replication (SMR).
Researchers utilized AI to aid in the discovery of 'A-greement,' a novel consensus protocol.
A-greement demonstrates significant performance improvements over existing state-of-the-art solutions for geo-replicated state machines.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags confirm its connection to key ML frameworks like transformers and the Llama family.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary application.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to major AI frameworks like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model designed specifically for persistent AI agents.
The model excels at multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million in a new funding round.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to a 90% speed increase based on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Meta’s AI could still scrape news sites, legal experts say
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Meta's recent updates to its business terms aim to curb the use of news sites for AI training.
Legal experts argue these changes are insufficient because ambiguous language still permits scraping.
The core concern remains Meta's ability to use content associated with its services for AI model training.

stories.title: The FCC is beginning to block gadgets with ‘foreign surveillance chips’
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: The FCC has gained new authority to block electronic gadgets containing chips deemed a threat to national security.
This power allows the FCC to ban devices based on the origin of their computer chips if they are on a designated threat list.
The FCC is exercising this new authority for the first time by blocking two specific gadgets due to 'foreign surveillance chips'.

stories.title: Meta shocked by $25B fine after N.M. refused to join multistate settlement
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta faces a massive $25 billion fine following a refusal by New Mexico to join a multistate settlement.
The imposed fine is noted as the largest one Mark Zuckerberg has personally faced.
Meta has indicated its intention to appeal the ruling.

stories.title: Hackers got a four-day head start on epic PHP2Shell vulnerability
stories.author: Tom Wilson and Rafe Rosner-Uddin, Financial Times
bullet_points: A critical PHP2Shell vulnerability was exploited by hackers before defenders were aware of it.
The story highlights the speed and proactive nature of threat actors in exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities.
This incident underscores the ongoing challenge of timely vulnerability disclosure and patching in web infrastructure.

stories.title: Environment Duels: A Microcosm of LLM Co-Evolution
stories.author: Mayur Naik
bullet_points: Introduces 'Environment Duels,' a novel agentic benchmark for evaluating frontier LLMs.
The benchmark tests LLMs' dual roles as both creators (writing environments) and solvers.
It simulates a real-world co-evolutionary ecosystem where models interact with each other's outputs.

stories.title: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
stories.author: Calvin Xiao
bullet_points: Introduces Quant-Arena, a new benchmark specifically designed to test LLM agents for end-to-end quantitative trading research.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluation by moving beyond scoring isolated formulas or decisions to testing the entire research loop (hypothesis -> signal -> testing).
Focuses on applying advanced LLMs to complex, real-world financial tasks, signaling a potential shift in how AI is used in high-stakes quantitative finance.

stories.title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
stories.author: Mike Zheng Shou
bullet_points: Introduces Multimodal Embodied Agents (MMEAs) as a unified framework bridging computer-use agents and robotic systems.
MMEAs are defined as goal-directed systems that integrate multimodal task reasoning with physical action and feedback loops.
The research addresses the fundamental shift in capabilities and challenges when moving AI agents from purely digital environments to physical, robotic ones.

stories.title: Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation with Preference Feedback
stories.author: Di Wang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical privacy vulnerability in Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) by incorporating Differential Privacy (DP).
The research tackles the limitation of existing private alignment methods, which are constrained by dense reward parameterizations.
Proposes a novel approach for Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation, aiming to reduce estimation error bounds dependent on model size.

stories.title: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
stories.author: Jianfei Chen
bullet_points: Introduces 'LongZero,' a method to enhance long-context reasoning in LLMs without relying on extensive, expensive training data.
Addresses the critical bottleneck in RL-based LLM improvement: the scarcity and cost of generating long, diverse, and verifiable training data.
Presents a novel approach to RL from zero data, circumventing the dependency on large external corpora or superior teacher models.

stories.title: Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation with Preference Feedback
stories.author: Di Wang
bullet_points: Addresses the privacy vulnerability in Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) by integrating Differential Privacy (DP).
The research tackles the limitation of existing private alignment methods, which assume dense reward parameterizations.
Proposes a method for Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation, aiming to improve error bounds independent of model size.

stories.title: Environment Duels: A Microcosm of LLM Co-Evolution
stories.author: Mayur Naik
bullet_points: Introduces 'Environment Duels,' a new dynamic agentic benchmark for evaluating LLMs.
The benchmark tests LLMs not only as solvers but also as creators within an interactive ecosystem.
It examines how frontier LLMs co-evolve by absorbing outputs from predecessors and competitors.

stories.title: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
stories.author: Calvin Xiao
bullet_points: Introduces Quant-Arena, a new benchmark designed to evaluate LLM agents on the full, iterative loop of quantitative trading research.
Addresses a gap in existing benchmarks by moving beyond scoring isolated formulas or decisions to testing end-to-end strategy generation.
Focuses on testing LLMs' ability to complete the entire research cycle: hypothesis generation, signal implementation, historical testing, and strategy refinement.

stories.title: What the Author Wrote, What the Agent Reads: Silent Cue Loss in Enterprise Document Ingestion
stories.author: Pradeep Kumar Misra
bullet_points: Identifies a critical, often overlooked failure point in enterprise AI document ingestion: the loss of semantic cues during text conversion (e.g., from PDF/Word to tokens).
Demonstrates that this 'silent cue loss' causes AI agents to make confidently incorrect decisions rather than simply failing to process information.
Proposes a new task based on real-world policy documents to quantify and address this information degradation in deployed enterprise agents.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud infrastructure.
This integration expands the capabilities of Ollama by adding a powerful, large-scale multimodal model.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection has released its first open-weight model, Beam, on Ollama.
Beam is specifically designed for software engineering, reasoning, and agentic tasks.
The model is currently available for free on Ollama Cloud for a limited duration.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the deployment of AI agents using its cloud models.
The integration allows these agents to run securely within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for safe and accessible deployment of AI agents.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of decision-making logic.
The models can process text to provide probabilistic answers for yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI interfaces with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Meta turns Muse sharing back on
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta has reinstated the sharing functionality for its AI assistant, Muse.
The re-enabling followed security researcher warnings about easily discoverable public conversation links.
Researchers demonstrated that sensitive pages, such as internal business reviews and loan applications, could be found via these links.

stories.title: Electric or gas? BMW goes both ways with new 2027 X5 and iX5.
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: BMW is offering a dual-powertrain strategy for the 2027 X5 and iX5.
The electric variant boasts a substantial 450-mile range.
The EV model supports a high-speed charging rate of 460 kW.

stories.title: Samsung all but confirms iPhone Duo is goosing Galaxy Z8 sales
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: iPhone Duo's unveiling coincided with a surge in searches for Samsung foldables.
The article suggests the new iPhone model is negatively impacting Galaxy Z8 sales.
This indicates increased competitive pressure in the premium foldable/smartphone market.

stories.title: PhysiCalWorld: In-Context Physics Calibration for World Models
stories.author: Jeong Joon Park
bullet_points: PhysiCalWorld addresses a critical limitation in world models: the inability to infer underlying physical properties (mass, friction, damping) from limited visual observations.
Current world models suffer from prediction drift in novel environments because they lack calibrated physical parameters.
The proposed method calibrates these physics factors in-context, aiming to improve the accuracy and generalization of world model predictions.

stories.title: BatchBench: Benchmarking AI Robustness to Batch Effects and Domain Shift in Biomedical Images - A JUMP Cell Painting Leaderboard
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces BatchBench, a new leaderboard specifically designed to benchmark AI robustness in biomedical imaging.
Addresses the critical issue of domain shift, where AI models fail when tested on data acquired under different experimental conditions.
Focuses on evaluating the performance of AI systems against batch effects, a persistent challenge in biomedical image analysis.

stories.title: AtomicRL: Atomic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
stories.author: Liang Lin
bullet_points: Introduces AtomicRL, a new approach combining Reinforcement Learning (RL) with Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for robotic manipulation.
Addresses key limitations in current VLA-RL methods, specifically delayed/biased credit assignment from sparse rewards and bottlenecks from imbalanced subtask mastery.
Focuses on improving the mastery of complex, long-horizon skills in robotic tasks.

stories.title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
stories.author: Jun Xu
bullet_points: Proposes Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for sequential recommendation systems.
Challenges the standard practice of allocating a fixed computational budget to all historical items.
Identifies that item computational needs are non-uniform, with some requiring deep processing while others converge quickly.

stories.title: BatchBench: Benchmarking AI Robustness to Batch Effects and Domain Shift in Biomedical Images - A JUMP Cell Painting Leaderboard
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces BatchBench, a new leaderboard designed to benchmark AI robustness in biomedical imaging.
Addresses the critical issue of AI susceptibility to domain shifts caused by varying experimental conditions in medical imaging.
Evaluates the performance of AI systems under batch effects and domain shift, highlighting persistent gaps in current domain adaptation methods.

stories.title: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
stories.author: Jianfei Chen
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of training Large Language Models (LLMs) for long-context reasoning without extensive, expensive, or scarce high-quality training data.
It proposes 'LongZero,' a method leveraging Reinforcement Learning (RL) from zero data to enhance LLM capabilities.
The work aims to overcome limitations in current RL approaches that rely on difficult-to-obtain human annotations or strong teacher models.

stories.title: Did the Problem Actually Get Harder? Testing LLMs on Paired P and NP-Complete Problems Hardened by Adversarial Multi-Agent Rewriting
stories.author: Shubhashis Roy Dipta
bullet_points: Introduces P2NPCBench, a new benchmark designed to test Large Language Models (LLMs) on the boundary between P and NP-Complete problems.
Addresses a limitation in existing benchmarks, which fail to distinguish between problems based on their computational complexity class.
Aims to evaluate if LLMs can truly 'reason' about problem structure rather than just recalling solutions, by pairing NPC problems with their polynomial-time (P) counterparts.

stories.title: GoiBERT: Compact Vietnamese Language Models via Two-Stage Knowledge Distillation
stories.author: Huynh Dai Nhan Tran
bullet_points: Introduces GoiBERT, a family of compact Vietnamese language models (26M and 49M parameters).
Addresses the deployment cost of large Vietnamese NLP models by operating directly on raw text without external segmentation.
Employs a two-stage knowledge distillation process using complementary teacher models for training.

stories.title: Looped Uniform Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Praneeth Vepakomma
bullet_points: Introduces Uniform Diffusion Language Models (UDLMs) for text generation via iterative denoising of corrupted tokens.
UDLMs feature a challenging training objective where they must denoise from potentially unreliable contexts, unlike Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs).
Despite being more FLOP-intensive to train than MDLMs, UDLMs demonstrate superior downstream reasoning performance.

stories.title: Agent Behavior Maps: Locating Agents by What They Would Do, Without Running Them
stories.author: Masafumi Oyamada
bullet_points: Introduces 'Agent Behavior Maps' to characterize LLM agents based on their potential actions.
Allows for the comparison of agent behaviors using centered action log-likelihoods without needing to run the target agent in a new environment.
Demonstrates that distance metrics derived from these maps correlate well with actual trajectory Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence across multiple models.

stories.title: OpenShell – A safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents
stories.author: niemandhier
bullet_points: Introduction of OpenShell, a runtime environment designed for autonomous AI agents.
The runtime emphasizes safety and privacy for managing fleets of AI agents.
The concept addresses the growing need for secure orchestration of multi-agent AI systems.

stories.title: Show HN: Run full iOS 16.5 firmware on Android Devices
stories.author: aghuang
bullet_points: A user shared a project demonstrating the ability to run full iOS 16.5 firmware on Android devices.
This represents a significant technical achievement in cross-platform emulation or firmware porting.
The topic is highly niche, appealing to advanced developers and low-level systems enthusiasts.

stories.title: Scaling stateful Gemini 4 Argon agent sessions on GKE: Connection draining, startup boost, and session persistence
stories.author: olivi-eh
bullet_points: Addresses the technical challenge of scaling stateful AI agent sessions (Gemini 4 Argon) on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE).
Proposes specific Kubernetes/GCP solutions, including VPA CPU startup boost and GCPBackendPolicy connection draining.
Focuses on operational concerns like session persistence and efficient resource management for long-running AI workloads.

stories.title: AI Made Coding Cheaper. So Why Is Building Software Still So Expensive?
stories.author: harsh2644
bullet_points: The article discusses the paradox of AI lowering coding costs while software development remains expensive.
It highlights the capability of AI tools to rapidly generate complex code components (e.g., authentication flows, database schemas, unit tests).
The core discussion centers on the gap between AI-driven efficiency gains and persistent high software development costs.
